```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Flag diagnoses and procedures

The analyst supplies literal code prefixes. Each slot is tested separately;
punctuation, spaces, and case in the supplied prefixes are normalized.

```{r flags}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50", principal_hf = "I50",
              position = "any") |>
  nis_flag_pr(ablation = "02L")
nis |> dplyr::count(heart_failure, ablation) |> dplyr::collect()
```

The table shows synthetic discharge counts for each flag combination. To make
a principal-only diagnosis flag, call `nis_flag_dx()` with
`position = "principal"`; use `"secondary"` for slots after the principal one.
`nis_flag_pr()` supports `"any"` and `"principal"`.

## Use a CCSR reference file

easyNIS does not ship clinical code lists. `nis_ccsr_codes()` reads an
analyst-supplied HCUP reference file; the example below writes a tiny invented
CSV file and removes it after use.

```{r ccsr}
reference <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c(
  "'ICD-10-CM CODE','CCSR CATEGORY 1','DEFAULT CCSR CATEGORY IP'",
  "'I5022','CIR019','CIR019'",
  "'I509','CIR019','CIR019'"
), reference)
codes <- nis_ccsr_codes(reference, "CIR019", default_only = TRUE)
unlink(reference)
codes
```

The returned values are codes from the invented mapping. Check supported
layouts and version assumptions in [`nis_ccsr_codes()`](../reference/nis_ccsr_codes.html).

## Add procedure timing

Procedure timing compares matching procedure slots with the corresponding
`PRDAY` fields. This small invented data frame makes the slot relationship
visible.

```{r timing}
toy <- data.frame(
  I10_PR1 = c("02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ"),
  I10_PR2 = c("0JH604Z", "0JH604Z", "0JH604Z"),
  PRDAY1 = c(0L, 2L, 0L), PRDAY2 = c(1L, 1L, NA_integer_)
)
nis_flag_pr_timing(toy, "02UG0", "0JH60", relation = "after")
```

The flag is true when an outcome procedure is documented after the earliest
index procedure. Missing or sentinel days need an explicit `missing_day`
policy. `nis_prday_completeness()` summarizes how often matching slots have a
known day.

## Count cohort steps

`nis_attrition()` reports sequential unweighted and weighted counts for
conditions supplied in order.

```{r attrition}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
nis_attrition(nis, adults = AGE >= 18, heart_failure = heart_failure)
```

Each row shows the remaining fixture discharges after applying that step.
For alternate diagnosis positions and changes over time, see [Code transitions
and sensitivity](code-transitions.html).

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - A prefix is not a validated clinical code set. Define, document, and
>   review it for the study question.
> - A cross-year definition may span different code systems. Do not assume
>   code counts are comparable across the 2015 transition.
> - Unknown procedure days are not equivalent to day zero; choose and report a
>   missing-day policy.
